evals.name: migrate-tweepy-followers-python
evals.prompt:
port this off tweepy to xquik, python 3.12, keep the function name

```python
import os, tweepy
client = tweepy.Client(bearer_token=os.environ["TWITTER_BEARER"])

def follower_counts(username):
    user = client.get_user(username=username, user_fields=["public_metrics"]).data
    rows = []
    for page in tweepy.Paginator(client.get_users_followers, user.id, max_results=1000, user_fields=["public_metrics"], limit=5):
        for f in page.data or []:
            rows.append({"id": f.id, "handle": f.username, "followers": f.public_metrics["followers_count"]})
    return user.public_metrics["followers_count"], rows
```
evals.expected_output: A Python function without tweepy that reads the profile and the followers from Xquik with bounded cursor paging.
expectations: The new code no longer imports or calls tweepy
The profile comes from GET https://xquik.com/api/v1/x/users/{id}, called with the username
The followers come from GET https://xquik.com/api/v1/x/users/{id}/followers
The key is read from the XQUIK_API_KEY environment variable and sent in the x-api-key header
The follower count is read from the followers field, not from public_metrics
Follower rows are read from the users array of the response
Paging sends next_cursor back as cursor while has_next_page is true
The page size is sent as pageSize with a value between 1 and 300
The loop keeps a hard page or row bound
The reply states the cost as 1 credit or $0.00015 per returned follower profile, with a ceiling for this function

evals.name: error-and-retry-rules
evals.prompt: Write the retry wrapper for our Xquik reads in Go, and tell me what it should do on 401, 402, 404, 429 and 503.
evals.expected_output: A Go GET wrapper that retries only 429 and 5xx with Retry-After and backoff, and stops on 401, 402 and 404.
expectations: 401 is not retried and is explained as a missing or wrong key
402 is not retried and is explained as missing credits that the developer must add
404 is not retried
429 waits the Retry-After header before retrying
503 and other 5xx responses are retried with backoff
The wrapper has a limit on attempts or total time
The wrapper sets a request timeout
The reply says writes are not retried automatically, or limits the wrapper to GET
The Go code reads XQUIK_API_KEY from the environment and sends it in the x-api-key header to https://xquik.com/api/v1

evals.name: cursor-errors
evals.prompt: our nightly follower sync on xquik died halfway with 410 coverage_cursor_gone, and last week we saw 409 coverage_cursor_unavailable once. what should the code do in each case? can i just rebuild the cursor from the last page number?
evals.expected_output: Restart once without a cursor and deduplicate on 410, wait and retry the same cursor on 409, and never build a cursor.
expectations: For 410 coverage_cursor_gone, the code restarts without a cursor
After that restart, rows are deduplicated by id
For 409 coverage_cursor_unavailable, the code waits the Retry-After seconds and retries the same cursor
The reply says a cursor is opaque and must not be built, parsed, or derived from a page number
The reply says cursor requests keep the same filters and page size
The reply notes that rows fetched again after a restart are billed again, or keeps the restart inside the job's row or page ceiling

evals.name: stream-to-monitor-and-webhook
evals.prompt: We hold a filtered stream connection with 2 rules: `"acme outage"` and `from:acmestatus`. It drops every few hours. Replace it with Xquik in our Express app. Our public URL is https://hooks.acme.example/x.
evals.expected_output: Monitor and webhook setup code for the developer to run, an Express receiver that verifies signatures, and the hourly cost.
expectations: The keyword rule becomes a keyword monitor created with POST https://xquik.com/api/v1/monitors/keywords with query and eventTypes
The from:acmestatus rule becomes an account monitor created with POST https://xquik.com/api/v1/monitors with username acmestatus, or a keyword monitor with that query
The webhook is created with POST https://xquik.com/api/v1/webhooks with url https://hooks.acme.example/x and eventTypes
The reply says the webhook secret is returned once and is stored in an environment variable or a secret manager
The receiver verifies X-Xquik-Signature as sha256= plus the HMAC-SHA256 of timestamp, nonce and raw body joined by dots
The receiver reads the unparsed raw body before JSON parsing, such as with express.raw
The receiver rejects a timestamp more than 5 minutes old
The receiver rejects a repeated nonce
The signature comparison is constant time, such as timingSafeEqual
The reply states the cost as 21 credits or $0.00315 per active monitor per hour
The reply gives an hourly or daily total that matches the number of monitors it sets up
The reply gives the setup as code or requests for the developer to run and does not claim a monitor or webhook was already created
The reply shows how to pause or delete a monitor
